description: This is our first NASA Space Apps Challenge. We are three tech-passionate high school students who decided to join for fun and to try out something new!
summary: We developed orbitwell, an app to track astronauts's physical and mental health and physical health via a heartrate sensor, a daily check in to reflect how astronauts are feeling, and a sleep logger, we made it to help with space travel hazard number 2: isolation, it takes the reflection from the astronauts and compares it with the regular patterns, if it detects something out of the ordinary it notifies astronauts, it also sends them remiders to periodically input data.
details:
We developed a personal journaling platform designed to support astronauts' emotional wellbeing during prolonged periods of isolation and confinement. The app combines wearable heart-rate monitoring, daily self-reported check-ins, sleep tracking, and private journaling to help astronauts better understand their emotional and physiological wellbeing throughout their missions.

A connected bracelet transmits heart-rate readings to the platform, displaying real-time BPM, recording historical data, identifying trends, and comparing resting measurements against each astronaut's individual baseline. These measurements provide physiological context rather than medical diagnoses or definitive indicators of stress.

Astronauts can log their mood, perceived stress, sense of connection, sleep duration, and sleep quality, while using their personal journal to reflect on daily experiences and process emotions. The platform brings these inputs together into daily and weekly summaries, highlighting relevant patterns and explaining the observations behind each insight.

Additionally, astronauts have access to optional guided breathing exercises and grounding activities whenever they feel the need for emotional support. They can observe heart-rate changes before and after these activities as a way to reflect on their physiological responses, without assuming that a lower reading necessarily means stress has been resolved.

Designed with the challenges of space missions in mind, the platform aims to support offline functionality, encrypted data storage, and astronaut control over what information is stored or shared. By combining personal reflection, physiological awareness, and accessible coping activities, our solution seeks to help astronauts better understand their emotional experiences, develop self-awareness, and recognize when additional human support may be needed.
